title: Grammarly vs QuillBot
intro: Grammarly and QuillBot are both popular writing tools with free plans, and they overlap on grammar checking. Their starting points are different, though: Grammarly is built around correcting and improving text as you write, while QuillBot is best known for rewriting and summarising text you paste in.
This comparison explains how they differ so you can pick the one that matches how you write. Many people use one of each.
similarities: Both offer a free plan and paid upgrades.
Both include grammar and spelling checking.
Both use AI to suggest changes to your text.
Both are used by students, professionals and content writers.

differences.a: Correcting and improving text as you write
differences.b: Paraphrasing and summarising text you provide

differences.a: Browser extension and apps that work inside other software
differences.b: Mainly its own web editor, plus extensions — check official site

differences.a: Write normally and accept suggestions inline
differences.b: Paste text, choose a mode, compare outputs

considerA: You want suggestions inside email, documents and web forms as you type.
Your main goal is correctness, clarity and tone rather than rewording.
You write a lot of short, everyday text such as emails and messages.
considerB: You often need to rephrase or simplify your own drafts.
You want to summarise long material quickly.
You prefer working in a dedicated editor rather than an extension.

faqs.q: Can I use Grammarly and QuillBot together?
faqs.a: Yes. Some writers paraphrase or summarise in QuillBot and then proofread the result in Grammarly. Check each tool's terms and your organisation's AI policy.
It depends on the task. Grammarly suits proofreading assignments; QuillBot suits summarising notes and rewording your own drafts. Always follow your institution's rules on AI tools.
